issues.description: Animal constructor signature/attributes are inconsistent between the specification and the reference solution. The UML/problem statement specifies Animal has fields `name: String` and `age: int` and a constructor `Animal(String, int)`, but the solution implements only `private String name;` and `public Animal(String name)` (no `age` field/parameter). This makes it unclear whether students must implement `age` and which constructor signature tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Align all artifacts: either (a) update the UML/problem statement to remove `age` and specify `Animal(String name)` only, or (b) update the solution to include `private int age;`, implement `public Animal(String name, int age)`, add getters/setters for both fields, and adjust all subclasses accordingly.

issues.description: Subclass constructor signatures are inconsistent with the UML/spec. The problem statement/UML implies `Seal`, `Pig`, and `Goat` constructors must initialize all Animal attributes (i.e., call `super(String, int)`), but the solution provides only single-argument constructors `Seal(String)`, `Pig(String)`, and `Goat(String)` calling `super(name)`. This cascades from the Animal age/signature mismatch and can block students if tests/spec expect an `age` parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: After deciding the intended Animal constructor, make subclasses match it: either keep everything as `(String name)` and remove `age` from the spec/UML, or change all subclasses to `(String name, int age)` and call `super(name, age)`.
